newsitem.title: USA: Heartport system used in triple bypass.
newsitem.headline: Heartport system used in triple bypass.

text.p: Surgeons at New York University Medical Center have performed the first triple-bypass heart surgery using Heartport Inc's minimally invasive technology, the university said Thursday.
In the operation on a 61-year-old man, surgeons used HeartPort's Port-Access technique to make one three-inch incision between the ribs, through which the heart was reached, turned and manipulated.
The system is one of the so-called minimally invasive surgical techniques that allow surgeons to operate on the heart without cracking open a patient's chest.
Researchers have said the surgeries, in addition to being less painful, result in shorter hospital stays and lower overall hospital costs.
The patient who underwent the triple-bypass port-access surgery expects to return to work on Monday, 11 days after his surgery, the university said.
The HeartPort system involves stopping the heart during surgery and placing the patient on a heart-lung machine.

Other minimally invasive techniques -- for which CardioThoracic Systems Inc, Medtronic Inc and U.S. Surgical Corp are developing surgical devices -- work on beating hearts and avoid the heart-lung hookup.
Proponents of the HeartPort system say that by stopping the heart, it facilitates doing multiple-vessel bypasses and other repairs such as valve replacements.
